verses.1: For the music director. A testimony for Asaph. A psalm.
verses.2: Shepherd of Israel, come near; the one who leads Joseph like sheep, the one who sits enthroned among the cherubim, appear!
verses.3: In the presence of Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your might, and come to our rescue.
verses.4: O God, restore us and reveal your face, and we will be saved.
verses.5: O Lord, God of hosts, how long will you be angry with the prayer of your people?
verses.6: You have fed them bread of tears, and given them tears to drink in abundance.
verses.7: You have made us an object of ridicule to our neighbors, and our enemies mock us.
verses.8: O God of hosts, restore us and reveal your face, and we will be saved.
verses.9: You brought a vine from Egypt, you drove out nations and planted it.
verses.10: You cleared the ground for it, and you caused its roots to take hold, and it filled the land.
verses.11: Its shadow covered the mountains, and its branches were like cedar trees.
verses.12: Its branches stretched toward the sea, and its roots reached to the river.
verses.13: Why have you broken down its walls, so that all who pass by the road strip it?
verses.14: A wild boar from the forest has ravaged it, and a beast of the field has devoured it.
verses.15: O God of hosts, come back now; look from heaven, see, and attend to this vine.
verses.16: And the vine you planted with your right hand, and the son you strengthened for yourself.
verses.17: Burned in fire, scorched, and from your rebuke it perishes.
verses.18: Let your hand be on the man you strengthened, on the son of humanity you fortified for yourself.
verses.19: Then we will not wander from you; revive us, and we will call on your name.
verses.20: O Lord, God of hosts, restore us and reveal your face, and we will be saved.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: "bread of tears" and "tears to drink in abundance" reflect the Hebrew's metaphorical and poetic language, capturing the sorrow and hardship described.
